html:
The imperial dynasty that ruled China from 618 to 907, often seen as the high point of Chinese civilisation. It was open, rich and cosmopolitan, and its capital, Chang'an, was perhaps the largest city in the world.

The Li family took power as the Sui collapsed. The second emperor, Taizong, conquered far into Central Asia, and Tang lands for a time reached further than the Han. The dynasty kept the Sui's Grand Canal and exams, and issued the Tang Code of law.

What made it famous:

  • Traders, monks and envoys from Persia, Central Asia, Korea and Japan crowded Chang'an along the Silk Road.
  • Xuanzang went to India and brought back Buddhist texts.
  • Poets such as Li Bai and Du Fu wrote the best-loved poems in Chinese.
  • Woodblock printing spread; the Diamond Sutra of 868 is the oldest dated printed book.

From 690 to 705 Wu Zetian ruled as emperor in her own name, the only woman to do so.

The turning point was the An Lushan rebellion of 755 to 763. It killed millions and left power with regional military governors. In 751 the Tang also lost to the Abbasids at the Battle of Talas in Central Asia. In 845 the court turned on Buddhism in the Great Anti-Buddhist Persecution. Peasant revolts in the 870s and 880s wrecked the empire, and in 907 a general deposed the last emperor, opening the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period before the Song.
sum: The imperial dynasty that ruled China from 618 to 907, often seen as the high point of Chinese civilisation. It was open, rich and cosmopolitan, and its capital, Chang'an, was perhaps the largest city in the world.
